titleStmt.title: Performability Comparison of Schedulability Conditions in Real-Time Embedded Systems

analytic.title: Performability Comparison of Schedulability Conditions in Real-Time Embedded Systems

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: In modern safety-critical real-time embedded systems, performance and reliability are two most important parameters. The joint consideration of these two parameters is called performability. This paper evaluates and compares different schedulability conditions, which are used for scheduling tasks with fault-tolerant Rate-Monotonic (RM) algorithm, with respect to their performability. The task reexecution scheme is used to implement fault tolerance in the RM scheduling algorithm. To evaluate the schedulability conditions, a software tool is developed to simulate an embedded processor with m schedulable periodic tasks. The results show that among five different schedulability conditions used in this evaluation, the best schedulability condition has on average 3.5% higher performability than the time the other conditions are used. Also, the simulation results show that the next best schedulability condition can on average increase the performability of the embedded processor 2.5% more than the other conditions.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Embedded real-time systems play an important role in our modern life and perform an ever-increasing number of computational and controlling applications [1]. Some of these applications such as controlling an avionic system, a medical system, or the braking system in a vehicle, have a kind of criticality in their nature and therefore need a high degree of reliability. This means that malfunctions in such systems may result in catastrophic consequences like harming the environment or human life. A common characteristic of these systems is the hard real-timeness, where the correct operation depends not only on the logical correctness of the results, but also on the time at which the results produced.

For the sake of clearness for the rest of current paper, three definitions are necessary, i.e., performance, reliability, and performability. Performance is defined as the probability of task completion within its deadline. In this definition the effect of task or processor failure is not embedded. Reliability is defined as the conditional probability of task correct run on the system during its runtime, given that in the beginning of task run, the systems is in fault free state [29]. Here, the task deadline is not important when only the reliability is considered. Performability is defined as the joint consideration of performance and reliability [22] [21] [14] [31] [27].

An important issue in real-time systems is the methods of task scheduling. Task scheduling is done by scheduling algorithms that determine at which instance of time tasks must be run [6] [16]. In other words, these algorithms determine the priority of tasks for running. These algorithms can be divided into two classes. One class is dynamic priority scheduling algorithms, where upon arrival of a task, the scheduling algorithm may change the priorities of already scheduled tasks. Two dominant dynamic scheduling algorithms are the Earliest-Deadline-First (EDF) and the Least-Laxity-first (LLF) [2]. The other class is the fixed priority algorithms, which are used to schedule periodic tasks; here the priorities of tasks are defined before the execution of tasks. The Rate-Monotonic (RM) algorithm is an example of the fixed priority algorithms, which is reported to be an optimal fixed priority algorithm [2] [13]. It is important to note that the fixed priority scheduling algorithms are usually used for task scheduling in hard realtime applications [5], which are ranked as a safety-critical application.

One common problem in all scheduling algorithms is that they cannot guarantee the tasks completion before their deadlines. This problem happens when a huge number of tasks are assigned to a processor. To solve this problem, the schedulability conditions are used to determine whether the assignment of a new task to the processor is feasible; if it is not feasible, the task will not be assigned to the processor at all.

The first attempt to derive such conditions was done by Liu and Layland [13], where a worst-case condition was developed. The main problem of this condition is its low processor utilization bound when the number of scheduled tasks approaches to infinity, which is reported as 69% of maximum processor utilization [7] [13]. Several attempts have been done to improve the utilization bound of this schedulability condition [4] [7] [15] [20] [24] [26]. In these studies, the utilization bound of the processor is improved; however, here the problem of measuring the performability of real-time systems is not addressed. When the ever increasing need of reliability in hard real-time embedded systems is considered, the performability measurement will be an overriding factor.

The fixed priority scheduling algorithms are widely studies in real-time literature, considering different aspects like performance, reliability and power consumption [3] [9] [12] [23]. Except the work [3] and [9], other studies are done without paying attention to the reliability or the performability requirements of the real-time systems. In [23], the issue of measuring the reliability of scheduling algorithms without considering the schedulability conditions is addressed. In [3] and [9], the performance of a faulttolerant real-time embedded system considering the schedulability conditions is obtained. However, in this work the performability of the system is not measured.

The present paper has two main contributions: 1) the performability of different schedulability conditions for the RM scheduling algorithms in a single embedded processor is studied, and 2) the effect of using different schedulability conditions on number of employed processors in a multiprocessor system is evaluated. To study and evaluate these conditions, a software tool is developed to simulate both single processor and multiprocessor real-time embedded systems. This tool can evaluate the performability and performance of different schedulability conditions for the RM scheduling algorithm. This evaluation is done by simulating an embedded system consisting of n processors and m primary tasks; in this experiment n=750 and m=1000. To tolerate tasks failures, the tasks are re-executed [23] if enough slack time is available.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows: Section two discusses the general partitioning techniques in multiprocessor systems, and the schedulability conditions for different implementations of RM algorithm. The issues of reliability and performability are explained in Section three. In Section four, the tasks models are discussed. The simulation methods and results are presented in Section five and six respectively. Finally, the conclusions are presented in Section seven.

div.head: II. TASK DISTRIBUTION AND SCHEDULABILITY
div.p: CONDITIONS On a multiprocessor system the tasks could be distributed either by the partitioning technique. In this technique, each instance of a particular task in the set (which is created by the partitioning technique) is executed on the same processor. Due to the intractability of optimal solution to the problem of partitioning [8], several heuristic methods for partitioning of tasks have been proposed; these methods are mainly based on the well-known bin-packing algorithms [4] [20]. In a multiprocessor system the task scheduling and distributing can be formed by combining any of the binpacking algorithms with any of the schedulability conditions for the RM algorithm. The schedulability conditions are defined as the necessary and sufficient conditions for checking whether the recently arrived task could be scheduled on a processor or not [2]. So distributing tasks among processors is done by the well-known bin-packing heuristic algorithms and the decision of whether a processor could accept the task or not is determined by the schedulability condition.

NF (Next-Fit), FF (First-Fit) and BF (Best-Fit) are three bin-packing heuristic methods. It could be derived from [3] and [9] that the Best-Fit method is the best way of task partitioning and processor selection in a multiprocessor system. The First-Fit is the next best method among these three methods. Depending on the results reported in work like: [3][9] [12], the First-Fit method has les implementation overhead and its performance is almost similar to the Best-Fit method. Thus, in the current evaluation, the First-Fit method is utilized. In addition five known schedulability conditions are used in current paper.

div.p: As it can be easily seen in the above mentioned schedulability conditions, the goal of designing and improving of such conditions is to guarantee the tasks completion before their deadline. Such conditions will guarantee that if they allow a task for being scheduled on a processor, it will meet its deadline. However, this guarantee is not for while, a task or a processor failure occurs. Therefore, measuring the probability of task on time completion (as a performance measure) without considering tasks failures is not appropriate for real-time systems. To do this, the performability is introduced as the joint consideration of performance and reliability.

div.head: III. RELIABILITY AND PERFORMABILITY
div.p: Reliability is one of the attributes that are encompassed with the dependability [10] and is defined as: the "continuity of correct service". Moreover, this term is defined as the conditional probability of task correct run (during its runtime), given that in the beginning of task run, the systems is in fault free state [29].

There are two main approaches to implement fault tolerance and consequently improve the reliability of tasks run in a real-time system. Both of These approaches are based on redundancy. In the first approach, time redundancy is used to tolerate faults [32]. To do this, upon detecting failure in a task, the task will be re-executed to produce correct results. If there is no slack time to re-execute the task, this approach fails. To remove this weakness, the checkpointing technique is introduced [32]. In this technique upon detecting a failure in the task, the task will rolls back to the previously captured checkpoint and continues its run to the end. By utilizing this technique there is more chance to finish task before the deadline, because the task won't restart from the beginning and with less slack time the task can produce the desired results successfully.

In the second utilizes the policy of running an identical copy of the task to achieve fault tolerance. This approach is called Primary-Backup scheme. This approach allows multiple executing of multiple copies of a task on different processors to tolerate processor(s) and task(s) failures [11] [18] [19]. In this approach, the main task is called primary and its identical copies are called backup tasks.

Primary-Backup Scheme is implemented in three ways [33]: a) Primary-Backup exclusive, where primary and backup tasks are mutually exclusive in processor and time. i.e., they run on different processors and on different times. b)

Primary-Backup concurrent, where primary and backup run at same time on different processors. c) Primary-Backup overlapping, where primary and backup run on different processors with overlap in their execution times. This is a combination from the first and second ways of implementing the primary-backup scheme. In current research, for implementing fault tolerance and improving the reliability of tasks the task re-execution method is used. If the failure detector detects a task failure, the system forces the task to be re-executed again if there is an enough slack time. As it mentioned above, in this scheme the task re-execution is on one processor. Hence, the processor failure could not be detected.

The other important measure in real-time systems is performance. Performance in current paper is defined as the probability of task completion within its deadline. Therefore, if the probability of task completion before deadline rises, performance of the system will be improved.

The definitions of reliability and performance have their own shortcoming. i.e., in reliability the task completion before the deadline is not considered and only the logical correctness of task results is important and in performance only the deadline is important and the issue of correct logical results is not significant. To remove this shortcomings, the joint consideration of performance and reliability is used, which is defined as performability. The performability in current work is defined and used as "the probability to complete the application correctly within its deadline in the presence of faults" [31] [27].

div.head: IV. SYSTEM MODEL
div.p: This paper evalutes the performability of a real-time embedded system for investigating the effects of using different schedulability conditions for the RM real-time scheduling algorithm. To do this, some models should be introduced.

div.head: A. Task Model
div.p: A set of n tasks { } The following assumptions are used in the task model: a) The arrivals of all tasks are periodic with constant intervals between arrivals. Thus, the task scheduling could be done offline by the RM scheduling algorithm.
b) It has been proven that the release times of tasks do not affect the schedulability of the tasks [13]. Therefore, release time i r can be omitted.
c) It is assumed that the deadline and period of each task are equal i i (d =T ).

d) The tasks are assumed independent from each other. e) Tasks are preemptible. i.e., upon arrive a task with higher priority, the current running task will release the processor and the newly arrived higher priority task will start its run and after finishing its run, release the processor for lower priority tasks.
f)
The tasks execution times are constant and is assumed that it is equal to the worst case execution time. g) There are sufficient resources in the system to avoid resource conflict tasks.

div.head: B. Architecture Model
div.p: One of the important parts of a multiprocessor system is its Communications links and communication protocols [25]. An unreliable Communications links and communication protocols will decrease the overall system reliability. There are some attempts to develop a highly reliable communication system for a dependable real-time system [28]. In this paper, the system is consisting of multiple homogeneous processors, which are connected via a reliable version of communication protocol such as CAN, TTP, Flexray, and etc [30].

div.head: C. Scheduler Modelin the multiprocessor system.
div.p: a) All the task arrives to a central processor, which is called dispatcher [16] [17].

b) The communication between the dispatcher and the processors is through dispatch queues. This is shown in Figure 1. c) Each processor has its own queue. The task, which are assigned to the processor place in this queue and wait for their turn for run. Here, the tasks turn is determined by the RM scheduling algorithms. d) Task dispatcher selects a processor with Best-Fit method and then determines whether the task schedulable with the processor or not. This decision is done by employing the schedulability conditions. e) The tasks assignment overheads are ignored. f)
The task re-execution mechanism is used to implement the ability of tolerating failures.

div.head: V. SIMULATION METHOD
div.p: In the first experiment, a single processor embedded system is simulated to study the effects of using different schedulability conditions on the system performability. To do this, the five schedulability conditions which are mentioned in Section two are utilized. The following steps are done for this simulation: a) A randomized initial task set is created. In generated set, the tasks have enough slack tame for reexecution upon detecting failure. Moreover, with lower task utilization, the schedulability conditions will enter their saturated mode and reveals their utilization bonds.

b) The schedulability conditions select the schedulable tasks sets depending on their conditions. c) The schedulable task sets simulates for over one million cycles and failures inject to the tasks. In this step the simulator re-executes the failed tasks.
d) The history of system run and the probability of task completion before the deadline are analyzed to measure the performability.

For the second experiment a homogeneous multiprocessor system like the Figure 1 is simulated to evaluate the effects of schedulability conditions on the performance of the system. Here, the performance is evaluated as the number of employed processors. For this evaluation an embedded system consisting of n processors and m primary tasks is simulated. For this experiment n=750 and m=1000.

These evaluations reveals the capabilities and weaknesses of the different schedulability conditions under the re-execution scheme in multiprocessor real-time systems; these capabilities and weaknesses will able the system designers to select a proper schedulability condition.

div.head: VI. SIMULATION RESULTS
div.p: Here, the simulation results of studying five schedulability conditions for the RM scheduling algorithm are presented. The results are shown in Table 1. In the first experiment, the performability is evaluated on a singe processor system. By this experiment, the effects of changing the schedulability condition are investigated on a real time embedded system.

As it could be seen from table 1, using different schedulability condition have different effect on the realtime embedded system. According to the simulation results, the second and forth schedulability condition have the same and the highest performability among the five simulated conditions. This result could be explained by the maximum utilization bound of each condition. For example the fifth condition is an improved condition, which has higher utilization bound from the first condition; therefore, the reexecution method has less chance to re-execute failed tasks while the fifth condition is used. However, the fifth schedulability condition uses less processor for task run in a multiprocessor environment. So the cost of process communication, management and power consumption reduces significantly. These results are drawn out by the second experiment. In this experiment a homogeneous multiprocessor system is evaluated to determine the effects of different schedulability conditions on the number of employed processors with a typical number of processors and tasks. As the results of this experiment, if a system designer need higher task performability this experiment recommends the forth schedulability condition and if he/she have a limitation on cost and number of used processors, it recommends the fifth condition. Also the designer could make a trade-off between performability and number of employed processor to choose other appropriate conditions.

The little differences between the performability of different schedulability conditions could have huge effects on the system performability and reliability [22]. It is important to note that in a safety-critical real-time embedded system like the controller of an avionic system, the processor reliability and performability are calculated as a part of a serial system like Figure 2. This means that the blocks performability are multiplied to each other to calculating the overall system performability and such systems needs a higher level of performability during their mission. In this paper, an evaluation of performability and performance for a real-time embedded system with five different schedulability conditions for the RM scheduling algorithms were presented.

To do this, a software tool was developed that can simulate an real-time embedded system consisting of n processors and m primary tasks, and an embedded system consisting of 750 processors and 1000 periodic tasks was simulated by the tool. The implementation of schedulability conditions on a multiprocessor system has been done by employing the Best-Fit method and then the performance of the different schedulability conditions in term of number of employed processor was evaluated. In addition, to implement fault tolerance, improving the reliability and studying the performability of the tasks, in a single processor real-time embedded system, the task re-execution method was used and then the performability of different schedulability conditions in term of the probability of correct run within the deadline and in presence of failure was measured.
The results show that among the five schedulability condition of the RM algorithm the forth condition [24] has the best performability and the fifth one [15] has the best performance.
